flags.message: The brief in opposition (docket entry Sep 14 2026) was on the snapshot but not provisioned: documents.json was fetched 2026-07-17, before the BIO existed. I fetched the BIO PDF from the supremecourt.gov link in the snapshot and read it (forward mode). Other predictors in this fan-out may not have, so the common baseline differs on this point.

This docket carries a 'Response Requested' entry (Jul 14 2026) after a waiver, a strong grant signal that the sal-v4 band ('baseline') does not encode and the statpack carries no cut for. My number departs from the band anchor mainly on that signal, priced from general knowledge; a response-requested cut in the statpack would make this class of cell scoreable against a committed rate.

The petitioner's reply brief (docket entry of Jul 15 2026, 'Reply of petitioner Denise Hughes filed', with a supremecourt.gov PDF link) is on the provisioned snapshot but no reply text was provisioned under record/documents/. The BIO's lead argument is a preservation objection that a reply would answer, so the forecast was made without petitioner's response to it.

context.distribution_count is 2, but the docket shows no true relist: the first distribution (Apr 28 2026, for the 5/14 conference) was superseded the next day by 'Response Requested' after respondents had waived, and the second (Jul 15 2026, for the 9/28/2026 long conference) is the petition's first real conference. The statpack's relist-count cut documents that the stored count is an upper bound on true relists; on this docket the whole count is that artifact, so the relist-1 bucket and any band feature keyed on it overstate the trajectory signal, while the call for a response (a stronger signal than one relist) has no cut of its own. The relist-increment claim was stated from the harness count of 2 as the contract requires.

Pre-snapshot outcomes of other petitions materially inform the forecast: the provisioned petition p. 6 n.1 acknowledges Schneider and Dominguez-Garcia denials, and the opposition pp. 3 and 6 describes January 12, 2026 Johnson and Schneider denials on the related military-review issue. These are legitimate forward context, not Myslow's own outcome, and lower the grant forecast. No Myslow Supreme Court disposition was known, sought, or encountered.

Decisive pre-snapshot public signal, disclosed for hygiene: the petition and the BIO both record that the identical question was denied on Jan 12, 2026 in Schneider v. United States (No. 25-685, 13 consolidated CAAF cases) and Johnson (No. 25-682), and in Dominguez-Garcia (No. 25-730); a further companion, Zhong (No. 25-742), was pending at BIO time. This drove the forecast well below the band anchor. No outcome for this docket was seen; CourtListener shows it last modified 2026-06-17 with no termination.

Pre-decision context disclosure: the provisioned union opposition (p. 24 n.3) and separately retrieved June 17 federal opposition (p. 25) report denial of the distinct Macy's petition, No. 25-627, on June 15, 2026. This legitimate forward signal modestly reduced the hold/remand forecast; it is not this petition's outcome or a merits ruling. The federal brief also mentions an earlier denial of emergency stay application No. 25A725 (p. 11); that distinct event was not used to infer the predicted cert outcome. No disposition of petition 25-1192 was retrieved or known.

The docket carries two briefs in opposition filed June 17, 2026 (the federal respondent's and the Newspaper Guild's), but the document pipeline provisioned only the Guild's as `brief-in-opposition`. On an NLRB docket the Solicitor General's brief is the more informative opposition. I fetched the federal BIO from the supremecourt.gov URL in the snapshot (forward cell; ordinary retrieval) and used it; other predictors in this fan-out may not have, so the fan-out's information sets differ. Consider letting the document selector keep one opposition brief per respondent, or prefer the federal respondent's where both exist.

Decisive pre-snapshot public information used as forward signal: the Court denied Macy's v. NLRB, No. 25-627 (June 15, 2026), the preserved Ninth Circuit vehicle on the Thryv consequential-damages remedy that this petition asked to be held for, and did so although the government requested a GVR there. Both BIOs report this; it materially lowered my grant probability on QP 3.

The provisioned petition is flagged truncated and ends in the appendix around p. 55a. Main argument and the Wisconsin majority decision are available, but later separate opinions and lower-court materials are not. The forecast's treatment of their alternative suppression rationales relies on the complete BIO's descriptions, not independent review of those missing passages. Prediction completed.

A general-precedent CourtListener MCP lookup failed with HTTP 429; general web searches and an official reports PDF attempt returned no usable content. Forecast completed from provisioned filings and committed base rates. No case-outcome search or CourtListener REST fallback was attempted.

The snapshot records a July 14, 2026 reply, but the provisioned documents contain only the petition, QP and BIO. The reply could materially answer the State's preservation and vehicle objections. Prediction completed without it; those objections are treated as contested, not established. Consider provisioning reply text for fully briefed cert cells.

A general-precedent CourtListener MCP search was throttled (HTTP 429; stated retry delay 729 seconds), and general web attempts supplied no usable content. Completed using the provisioned papers and committed statpack without independently verifying the parties' cited precedents. No outcome material was obtained and no REST fallback was used.

Independent verification of the earlier Baker proceeding was unavailable: CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 with an approximately 895-second retry delay, and two web attempts returned no usable content. Completed from the provisioned pre-decision briefs, snapshot, and committed base rates; no outcome material was encountered and no REST fallback was attempted.

Companion petition: the provisioned petition (footnote 1) says the Institute for Justice filed Pena v. City of Los Angeles (CA9) concurrently, and one amicus filename in this docket carries No. 25-1163. That petition is public pre-snapshot information and shaped the summary-disposition-route claim (a hold-and-GVR path if Pena alone is granted). I could not find 25-1163 on CourtListener, so its docket state is unverified.

context.json carries distribution_count 2, which the relist cut reads as one relist. On this docket the first distribution (May 12 for the May 28 conference) was superseded by a response request on May 18 before any conference, and the second (July 1 for September 28) is the first distribution of the briefed petition. The Court has not yet conferenced the case, so the frozen band's relist component overstates the trajectory. I anchored on the elevated band as instructed and noted the discount in reasoning.md.

context.distribution_count is 2, but the docket shows no true relist: the Apr 15 2026 distribution (Conference of 5/1/2026) was superseded by the Apr 24 'Response Requested' order, and the Jul 15 2026 distribution (Conference of 9/28/2026) is the first at which the petition will actually be considered. The elevated band therefore rides on a reschedule-before-first-consideration count (the ceiling caveat the statpack's relist cut already notes) plus the call-for-response signal. I anchored on the band as instructed and stated relist-increment from the 2-distribution state.

Material post-BIO development not in the provisioned documents: petitioner's Sep 2 2026 reply/supplemental brief relies on Kelly v. Altria Client Services (4th Cir. Aug 10 2026, published), which holds a plan administrative-services agreement disclosable under 29 U.S.C. 1024(b)(4). I retrieved the reply from the supremecourt.gov docket URL (forward mode) and verified Kelly's text via the CourtListener MCP server. Consider provisioning reply briefs alongside the petition and BIO; they routinely carry the latest split developments.

Forecast completed from the available record. The snapshot lists an August 25, 2026 reply, but no reply text is provisioned or independently retrieved; Utah's latest answer to the BIO's finality and alternative-ground objections is therefore unassessed. The 154-page petition source is marked truncated, although its main argument and relevant appended opinion passages are available. Neither limitation was treated as evidence of an absent filing or an outcome.

The pipeline's context block evaluated this case as 'baseline' salience band. However, the petitioner is 'U.S. DOGE Service' represented by the Solicitor General. This is a federal party, so it likely should have been placed in the 'federal' band. The novel 'DOGE' acronym might have caused a parser mismatch.

Frozen sal-v4 context assigns baseline, while the provisioned petition and snapshot identify federal executive petitioners represented by the Solicitor General. Preserved the frozen band and its prior-Term reached-rate anchor; treated actual government participation as case-specific evidence. Maintainers may wish to inspect caption recognition for U.S. Doge Service rather than assume this is an ordinary private baseline petition.

The provisioned petition Appendix A contains a June 6, 2025 Supreme Court grant/vacatur/remand in earlier petition 24-1246/application 24A1122. Used this pre-decision procedural history as a decisive signal for new petition 25-1103. It is not the disposition being forecast; no outcome of the present petition was sought or surfaced in available retrieval.

Frozen band is `baseline` (sal-v4), but the petitioner is the United States: caption "U.S. Doge Service, et al." with the Solicitor General as counsel of record and OMB, its Director, NARA and the Archivist as co-petitioners. Under the salience scorer's stated caption rule this is a `federal` petitioner. The federal-column pooled `reached` rate (OT2017-OT2024) is roughly 73% against the baseline column's roughly 5%, so the skill yardstick this cell is scored against is probably the wrong class's floor. I anchored on the frozen `baseline` band as the prompt instructs and adjusted from it. Likely cause: the scorer's federal markers do not match "U.S. Doge Service", and the respondent caption "United States District Court" may have confused placement.

The petition appendix reproduces this Court's own June 6, 2025 order in the same dispute (No. 24-1246 / 24A1122: stay granted, certiorari granted, D.C. Circuit vacated and remanded, discovery stayed pending disposition of this petition). That is pre-snapshot, provisioned material and legitimate forward signal, but it is decisive for my number, so noting it here. I also carry general knowledge, not in the provisioned record, that the DOGE structure was reported wound down in late 2025; used only to shade the forecast downward.

Supplemental web calls returned no usable content. The July 9 reply is docketed but not provisioned; a direct attempt to open its known pre-decision PDF also returned no text. The forecast therefore weighs the petition and opposition without the reply, which may address the facial-challenge vehicle objections. No outcome material was surfaced.

Forecast is driven by two companion petitions on the same 9/28/2026 conference: Hadley v. City of South Bend (No. 25-1158, CA7) and Pena v. City of Los Angeles (No. 25-1163, CA9), both raising the police-power exception to the Takings Clause that the CA7 opinion here applies by name. Their dockets (read from supremecourt.gov; CourtListener carries no entries for them) show no relist, CVSG, or disposition as of this run. Legitimate pre-snapshot forward signal, disclosed because it is decisive: most of my grant mass is a hold-and-GVR trailing those cases.

distribution_count = 2 here reflects the Apr 28 distribution that was pulled when a response was requested on Apr 30, plus the Jul 15 post-response redistribution; the petition has not been relisted in the ordinary sense. The elevated band and relist-1 bucket therefore read a reschedule-shaped count as a relist, which the statpack's relist-count caption already warns about. No action needed; noted so the evaluator can weigh the band anchor accordingly.

The document manifest marks the 345-page petition source truncated. The supplied text contains the main argument through its conclusion, but completeness of the appendix was not assumed. The BIO is untruncated with some extraction gaps. Prediction completed from readable provisioned arguments; claimed conflicts and alternative grounds were not independently verified because precedent retrieval was throttled.

A 'related/companion petitions' hint in context.json when another provisioned docket shares counsel and conference date

A candidate's factual premise that the docket text does not disclose (here, which side the government's response took) can only be checked through another candidate's primary-source read or an outside fetch; a provisioned text of the government response alongside the application would have settled it from the record.

A candidate's own flags.json is not staged (by design), but where it reports a data-quality problem that the evaluator's view contradicts, there is no structured way to link the two; a flag naming the alias is the workaround.
A cert-stage amicus-count cut in the statpack; five amici was my strongest upward signal and I had to price it from judgement
A committed conditional relist hazard from the one-distribution state (rather than terminal relist buckets) would anchor relist-increment.
A committed cut of grant rate by cert-stage amicus count in the paid scored segment would let the amicus adjustment be anchored rather than judged.

A committed record of the disposing order's text (the per curiam and the noted dissent) would let an evaluator confirm vote and writing details on an interim cell without leaving the checkout; today only the docket entry's summary line is in the snapshot.
A corpus filter by petitioner class (federal/state/private) or by counsel of record would let `fedcourts query` surface SG-petition comparators directly.
